A best practice guide for buying Linux games - GamingOnLinux.com
Not sure how many of us here are Linux gamers, but as one myself, I found this an interesting read.

Don't pre-order based on proclaimed Linux support. Too many developers are name-dropping Linux, SteamOS, Vulkan, etc., just to get extra pre-order dollars, then walking it all back after release. If you want to crowdfund, that's fine -- I do it, too. But don't drop cash on pre-orders just because the dev says they're going to support Linux.

Wait until the game drops; check it out; maybe buy it on Steam, where you have a reasonable refund policy. If you pre-order, and then six months later the dev delivers a game that only runs in Windows, putting Linux on a back-burner that never gets any attention, then you have no recourse.

Save your money: no tux, no bux.

Couldn't agree more.

I never pre-order games. I learned the hard way that promises cannot be trusted. Now I wait until I see others using a game on Linux to know it is properly supported, or if I see a Linux review from some of the Youtube Linux channels I frequent.
